## Italy’s Christmas sweet bread, explained


Panettone is a tall, dome-topped Italian sweet bread from Milan, traditionally made with raisins and candied orange and citron. It’s leavened with a natural sourdough starter and rises over several days, which gives it a light, airy, almost cotton-like texture. Panettone is the classic Italian Christmas and New Year’s dessert, and today it’s popular around the world, especially in Italian-American communities and across South America.

**Panettone at a glance**


- **What it is:** a tall, sweet, yeast-leavened bread enriched with butter, eggs, and sugar
- **Traditional fillings:** raisins and candied orange and citron
- **Where it’s from:** Milan, Italy
- **How it’s made:** with a natural sourdough starter and a rise that takes several days
- **When it’s eaten:** Christmas and New Year’s
- **How to say it:** pan-eh-TOE-neh
- **Popular variations:** chocolate, pistachio, Nutella, limoncello, and pear and chocolate


## **** **** **** **What is Panettone and How is it Made?**


[Panettone](https://www.goldbelly.com/foods/panettone) is an Italian sourdough yeast-leavened sweet bread from Milan, Italy. The sweet bread’s name is derived from pan del Ton, Italian for “Toni’s bread.” It is traditionally made with rum-soaked raisins and citron.


This Italian pastry has been eaten since the Middle Ages. True panettone is authenticated by the Italian government to ensure it’s made the traditional way with 16% butter and 20% candied fruit.


Ubiquitous at Christmastime, this iconic Italian dessert takes several days to make. First, the dough is cured and then it is proofed for two to three days. Then, dried citrus fruits and raisins are added. The result post-baking is a light and fluffy cylindrical **[sweet bread](https://www.goldbelly.com/foods/sweet-breads)** with a domed shape that is taller than its width.


Panettone is not to be confused with[pandoro](https://www.goldbelly.com/angelina-bakery/pandoro-classico) . Pandoro is an Italian sweet bread from Verona that resembles the Italian Alps in shape and look. Pandoro is a tall, eight-pointed star-shaped cake dusted with icing sugar.


## **** **** **** **** **How to Eat Panettone**


Panettone is often sold festively wrapped in cellophane or in a box. First, unbox and unwrap the bread. The round pastry typically has a paper wrapper covering its sides. Use a serrated knife — the same you would use to cut bread — to cut the loaf.


Start from the center and slice like you would a piece of pie. It can be tricky to cut panettone, so aim for tall, thin, triangular slices. It may be easier to cut when the paper liner is still on it. Be sure to remove the paper before serving.


Panettone is traditionally served alone as a dessert with a glass of sweet wine. It can also be served with mascarpone, crème anglaise, or Nutella. Many Italians enjoy a slice of panettone as a snack and even toasted panettone for breakfast during the holidays. Wrap up any leftovers to keep the air out. When stored properly panettone can stay moist and fresh for at least one month.


## **** **** **** **** **** **How to Pronounce Panettone**


Panettone is a four-syllable Italian word. Panettone is pronounced pan-net-TOW-neh, with the emphasis on the third syllable.

## **Panettone FAQ**


**Is panettone bread or cake?**


Both. It’s made like a bread, with yeast and a long rise, but it’s rich and sweet like a cake.


**What does panettone taste like?**


Panettone is light, airy, and buttery, with sweet raisins, bright candied citrus, and often a hint of vanilla.


**Why is panettone eaten at Christmas?**


Panettone has been a Christmas bread in Milan for centuries. Its rich ingredients, like butter, eggs, and dried fruit, made it a special-occasion treat.


**How do you store panettone?**


Wrap it tightly and keep it at room temperature. Toast slices or make French toast once it starts to dry out.
